text: At last night’s rehearsal in the Halewyn Civic Hall, the Halewyn Philharmonic introduced Greta Oyelaran as its new conductor, replacing Emil Voss after his final season ended in May. I saw Oyelaran step onto the podium shortly before 7:30 p.m., where board chair Lian Mercer welcomed her to the orchestra in front of about 60 musicians, staff and donors. “We’re ready for a sharper, brighter sound,” Mercer told me afterward. Oyelaran, 41, said she had already begun planning the September concert cycle and would open with Darnell Pike’s River Tides on 14 September. Several players said the first rehearsal felt “calm” and “focused,” and the brass section noted her precise, clipped beat.
